summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported on the August 17, 1869 fight between Tom Allen and Charley Gallagher at Foster's Island; the sponge was thrown up and Allen claimed victory, but the referee called it a draw.

metadata.notes: Page masthead reads 'The Missouri Republican--St. Louis, August 18, 1869.'

facts.fact: The paper gave Allen's birth as Birmingham, England, April 23, 1840 (aged twenty-nine)
Allen began fighting at twenty-one; in 1861 he beat Morris Connor for $25 a side in twelve rounds
In 1861 Allen beat White for $25 a side in eight rounds
In 1862 Allen beat Gould for $75 stakes in thirty-one rounds
In 1862 Allen lost to Posh Price for $100 a side in forty rounds
About 1864 Allen beat Bingy Rose for $250 a side in ten rounds
About 1864 Allen lost to Bob Smith, the Black, for $25 a side after three hours and twenty minutes
In 1865 Allen beat Jack Parkinson for $250 a side in fifteen rounds
In 1866 Allen beat Posh Price in a rematch, fifty-eight rounds for $250 a side
In 1866 Allen beat George Iles for $500 a side in eighteen rounds
On March 5, 1867, Allen fought Joe Goss for the championship and $2,000 a side; the fight ended in a draw
After the Goss draw Allen emigrated from England to America
In 1869 Allen beat Bill Davis in forty rounds for $1,000 a side
Soon after the Davis fight, Charley Gallagher beat Allen in two rounds for $1,000 a side (February 1869)
On June 15, 1869, Allen beat Mike McCoole in nine rounds for $1,000 a side but did not receive the stakes
Allen was described as about five feet ten and a half inches tall and 170 pounds in fighting trim
On July 13, 1869, Allen and Gallagher made a rematch for $500 a side and the excursion money, to be fought August 17 within fifty miles of St. Louis
On August 17, 1869, Allen fought Charley Gallagher at Foster's Island, 22 miles down the Mississippi from St. Louis, with Leary Wessel as referee
The sponge was thrown up in the Allen-Gallagher fight and Allen claimed the victory, but the referee decided the fight a draw
